owner.occupation: Home cook starting a small Afghan catering business

world.bio: I came from Kabul in 2021 with my husband and two children. I cook for every community gathering in Dandenong, weddings, funerals, Eid, school fundraisers, and now people are asking me to cook for their events and pay me. I want to turn it into a registered business but the rules are a maze. My kids are at the local primary school and I am studying for my citizenship test.
skills_assets: Cooking for 50 to 200 people: mantu, qabuli pulao, bolani, ashak, aush
A network of about 300 families in the Afghan community in Dandenong and Springvale
A large home kitchen with a domestic oven; two big pots, six trays; a second-hand stand mixer
Food handler certificate (Level 2), completed last year
Some English; improving. I can write recipes and do pricing in a spreadsheet
A Facebook page with 1,100 followers, photos of the food

projects.name: Registering the business
projects.text: I want to sell food through events and weekend orders. The council told me I cannot sell food cooked at home; I need a registered food premises. Renting a commercial kitchen costs $45 an hour. For a pilao for 100 people I need about six hours. That's $270 in rent before I buy rice and meat.

projects.name: Citizenship test
projects.text: Studying every night after the kids sleep. I'm on the chapter about Australian democracy. The vocabulary is hard but I like the questions about values.

projects.name: Sister's visa
projects.text: My sister's visa application is stuck in processing. She is in Pakistan. I check the immigration site every day.

notes.text: Cooked mantu for a school fundraiser, 150 pieces. The teachers asked for the recipe. I said it is my mother's. They said you should sell it. I said I'm not allowed.
Council email came again: 'Domestic kitchens cannot be used for commercial food sales.' I read it three times with a dictionary. Not a surprise but my chest felt tight.

Looked at commercial kitchens in Dandenong. One is $45 an hour with a three-hour minimum, another is $60 and has a waiting list. I cannot afford it without customers, and I cannot get customers without selling.

My father had a heart attack years ago in Kabul; for years I cooked low-salt for him. No fried onions, little oil, steamed fish. People think Afghan food is heavy, but I know how to make it light. I thought of that today when the school nurse asked about food for a child with a heart condition.
Eid party at the community hall: I cooked for 80 people. Everyone said they'd pay if I had a shop. I smiled and said inshallah.
Citizenship test mock: scored 17 out of 20. My husband scored 18. He teased me. I teased him back.
Kids' school mother said, Zahra, can you cook for my father? He is 74 and has diabetes. I said yes, of course. She offered to pay. I said let us talk after I fix the licence.
My sister called. The visa case officer asked for more documents. We are sending them tomorrow.
Husband said, we can use our savings for the kitchen rental. I said no. That's for the children.

messages.text:
Officer: Domestic premises cannot be used for sale of food. You may apply for a Class 3 food premises registration.
Me: What is needed?
Officer: A commercial kitchen layout and a food safety supervisor.

Nargis: Zahra, will you cook for my son's engagement? 60 people.
Me: I would love to. Can I do it in your kitchen?
Nargis: Yes, come on Friday.

Sarah: My dad loves your bolani. Could you make some for his birthday?
Me: Of course. How many people?
Sarah: Eight.

Sister: They want the bank statements.
Me: I will send them tonight.
Sister: Thank you, I'm scared.
